trussStatic.explanation: Assess linear elastic planar truss networks: signed axial force and stress, deflection, support reactions and named serviceability limits.
pitfalls: Nodes carry geometry and independent Cartesian restraints; members carry E and area, allowing redundant and mixed-stiffness structures.
Host direct stiffness checks stability before execution and independently verifies all native displacements, axial responses and reactions.
Fresh-process reconstruction reads the retained model; this is not a native database persistence claim.

examples.purpose: Triangular pin/roller truss with literal hand-calculation witnesses.

fields.explanation: Describe one complete pin-jointed structural network, its physical stiffness, nodal loads and measured limits. The result is a linear elastic axial assessment; it does not certify stability or safety.
fields.units: SI m, N, Pa and m²

/properties/version.explanation: Select the Schemaxis planar truss document contract. Keep schemaxis.opensees/1; this is separate from the native OpenSees engine version.

/properties/operation.explanation: Choose trussStatic for one full static nodal-load increment of an elastic planar network. Bending and time-dependent response are outside this operation.

/properties/nodes.explanation: List every physical joint once, with global coordinates and translation restraints. Members sharing a node ID share a pin joint; geometric crossings alone do not join members. Array order defines one-based node indices in the CSV.

/properties/nodes/items.explanation: One pin joint carries its x/y position and optional zero-translation restraints. Every joint must belong to at least one member; brace each component sufficiently to prevent free mechanisms.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/id.explanation: Name this joint with a unique lowercase identifier, such as apex. Member endpoints, nodal loads and displacement requirements refer to this exact ID; numeric CSV indices follow node array order.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/x_m.explanation: Global horizontal coordinate of the undeformed joint in metres; negative coordinates are allowed. Use the same coordinate frame for every node and force. Coincident member endpoints are rejected.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/y_m.explanation: Global vertical coordinate of the undeformed joint in metres. Coordinates describe the original small-deformation geometry, not a prescribed displacement.

/properties/nodes/items/properties/fixed.explanation: Two Boolean restraints in x then y order: [true,true] is a pin support and [false,true] is a vertical restraint. Omission means [false,false], a free joint. Supports impose zero translations, not rotations or settlements.
Set true to hold this global translation at zero or false to leave it free. The first entry acts in x and the second in y; both entries are required when the pair is supplied.

/properties/members.explanation: List straight axial bars with endpoints, Young's modulus and cross-sectional area. This permits arbitrary bounded triangular, redundant and mixed-stiffness networks; it does not create bending stiffness. Array order maps one-based member CSV indices.

/properties/members/items.explanation: One two-node straight elastic axial bar. Positive force is tension and negative force is compression. Compressive stiffness remains elastic; no buckling, slackening, yielding or bending check is implied.

/properties/members/items/properties/id.explanation: Give this bar a unique lowercase ID, such as diagonal_left. Force/stress requirements select this ID. Node IDs belong to a separate namespace.

/properties/members/items/properties/a.explanation: ID of the first endpoint joint. It must name an existing node and differ from b. Reversing a and b preserves the tension-positive force convention.

/properties/members/items/properties/b.explanation: ID of the second endpoint joint. Members join only through explicit shared endpoint IDs. Combine coincident parallel bars into an equivalent axial stiffness rather than duplicate endpoint pairs.

/properties/members/items/properties/you.explanation: Elastic axial Young's modulus of this member in pascals, such as 2e11 for a steel-like elastic study. Its product with area determines axial rigidity; do not enter GPa values without converting to Pa.

/properties/members/items/properties/are.explanation: Uniform member cross-sectional area in square metres, such as 0.001. Axial stiffness is E times area divided by length. Increasing area lowers elastic strain/stress in determinate bars but can redistribute force in redundant networks.

/properties/loads.explanation: List resultant global point forces at joints, with at most one entry per node. Superpose loads at the same node before authoring. At least one component must be nonzero; gravity/self-weight and distributed loads are not added automatically.

/properties/loads/items.explanation: One nodal point-force resultant acting in the undeformed global frame. Loads at supports are permitted and contribute to support reaction balance.

/properties/loads/items/properties/node.explanation: Existing node ID receiving this force. Use one force pair per loaded node; unlisted nodes receive zero applied force.

/properties/loads/items/properties/force.explanation: Two signed force components [Fx,Fy] in newtons. Positive x is right and positive y is up; [0,-1000] applies a 1kN downward point load. Both components are required.
Signed component of a global nodal point force in newtons, first x then y. Zero is allowed. Never enter kilonewtons without converting to newtons.

/properties/requirements.explanation: Optional named maximum measurements used to accept or reject the analysed design. Omission means no user performance limits; independent numerical/stability checks still apply. A failure preserves observed values and margins for explicit redesign.

/properties/requirements/items.explanation: One accountable maximum measurement at a named node or member. The measured magnitude must not exceed maximum. These are serviceability/elastic measurements, not code-compliance, yield or buckling certification.

/properties/requirements/items/propertie.explanation: Unique lowercase label identifying this design decision, such as apex_serviceability. It appears with the observed measurement and signed remaining margin in the assessment.

Choose displacement_m for the node translation-vector magnitude, force_N for absolute member axial force, or stress_Pa for absolute member axial engineering stress. Signed values remain in the result tables.
For displacement_m, name an existing node ID; for force_N or stress_Pa, name a member ID. Do not use numeric CSV indices or a node for a member quantity.

Nonnegative maximum acceptable magnitude in the selected quantity's SI unit: metres for displacement, newtons for force or pascals for stress. This is an explicit user decision; it never changes itself to make a run pass.
